title: Russ Morgan, Charlie Horvath and a first arrangement for Goldkette
summary: Russ Morgan took him to meet manager Charlie Horvath, who asked for a trial arrangement; Challis explains the Goldkette bands around Detroit.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional

blocks.x: Now, let me see, well, I went up one Sunday. We had Sunday off and they were working on Sunday in Detroit, it didn't make any difference. I think Monday was the night they had off, so I went down there and little old home week. Talking to Russ and Fuzzy and Itzy, they were in the band, and I met Jimmy then. So Russ took me down in the cellar, in the Greystone Ballroom, Charlie Horvath, the manager, his office was down in the cellar, way back in the back, so we went down there and he said, "I want you to meet this guy," and he went down talking
to -- we went down and talked to Charlie and Russ said, "Why don't you have this guy make some arrangements for you? He can write$."

This is Russ, yes. He was from Nanticoke. I should mention that. And I had played with him at one or two jobs when the Sirens put on some extra men and he was playing, he and Fuzzy Farrar at the Armory, Scranton Armory, so and besides I knew him when he played a couple of jobs around Wilkes Barre, you know, admired his work, his trombone playing and all this (inaudible).

So I never played with him too much, but I knew him and I played with him a few times, but he was conducting the band then. He wasn't playing with the Goldkette band, they had Bill Rank and Spiegel (Newell Willcox -- ed.) and he said, "Why don't you have this guy make some arrangements for you?" he said to Charlie, and he said, "Okay, what do you want to do."

Well, they left me with something to do, I don't know what it was, to tell you the truth, I can't remember but I think it was one of those things like "Ave Maria," something. One of those standards, semi-classic things and anyway, I was going to do it after I got home and send it in. And so I find out that I did -- Tommy was playing down in the Book-Cadillac, Jean had a band in the Book-Cadillac Hotel under Owen Bartlett.
He was a contractor as well.

Oh, he had a lot of bands. He had jobs all around Detroit. But his main ones were the Greystone band is where the one band played and then the other one was the Book Cadillac band, and Owen Bartlett had that, and then he had other little hotels and he free-lanced, he had a job here and a job there and well, you wouldn't remember, but at that time there was a lot of work around, lot of dances, lot of things being done, but -- so I figured I had made a contact and I got home and I wrote out an arrangement. I still had a lot of time before I would go to --
